impact:
## What is wrong

`createPin` (src/snapshot/store.ts:3225) validates ONLY the pin document. Verified by reading it: assertGuardedAuthority(authority) then detachDocument(pin, "pin", ...) then assertArtifactId("pin", doc.pinId) then assertPinInvariants(doc, path, pinId) then commitArtifact(...). Nothing in that chain reads doc.generationId against the store. A pin naming a generation that does not exist, is a symlink, has the wrong mode, has a malformed envelope, or fails its checksum is written successfully and reported as success.

The store's own comment says "Pins are hints: losing one costs a cursor a typed error", and GC is consistent with that: store.ts:3153 treats a pin as collectable when its generation id is absent from existingGenerations (built at :3070). So the shipped behaviour is coherent FOR THE STORE. The defect is at the seam a later decision created.

## Why it matters now

N-008 5a puts a pin-request path on T-011's control socket and says the SERVICE "validates and executes createPin, returning the pin id or a typed refusal". No single operation lets it validate atomically:

- createPin does not check the generation, as above.
- readGeneration (store.ts:2806) NOW EXISTS — landed by T-026 in commit 9524902 — but it authorizes only generations that are ALREADY pinned or manifest-retained, so it cannot validate an unretained generation BEFORE the pin that would authorize it exists. That circularity is unchanged by its landing.
- Service code re-implementing envelope / mode / checksum / container-race validation duplicates store internals outside the module that owns them.

Result: the service can return a pin id for a generation that can never be read. The reader's next call fails with a typed error and the pin it holds is worthless, which is a success answer that was not true when it was given.

## Impact

Blocks the ATOMIC form of T-011's pin-request path, and therefore the strongest form of T-013 AC 4. It does NOT block T-011 — see the reduction below, which is now implementable.

## CORRECTION 2026-08-04 — the reduction first proposed here was itself unsound

This issue originally said T-011 could ship a reduced form: "pin only generations named in the validated manifest's retention set ... sound because the retention set names generations the store's own publish protocol wrote and which GC is required to protect".

**That is wrong, and it is this project's recurring substitution class in new clothes: a value proven to have one property, then used as though a different property had been proven.** Manifest retention proves the generation is PROTECTED FROM GC. It does not prove the artifact is READABLE. The proof that they are different properties is in the store itself: `readSnapshot` separately opens, mode-checks, decodes, checksum-validates and runs generation invariants for every referenced id, and that work exists precisely because manifest membership establishes none of it. After startup a retained artifact can be removed, re-moded, replaced or corrupted while the manifest stays valid and its id stays in the retention set.

So the reduced form returns success for an unreadable generation in exactly the case this issue was filed about. Refuted by codex review of the T-011 re-plan revision 3, finding 3; the premise was checked against `readSnapshot` before recording the correction.

**What is actually reducible:** pin only a generation an existing store read has just returned as USABLE — normally the active generation — and create the pin inside the same serialized mutation bracket. Anything wider than that needs the store operation below.

## AMENDMENT 2026-08-05 — the licensed reduction is now IMPLEMENTABLE; the issue stays open

`readGeneration` (store.ts:2806) landed in commit 9524902 (T-026) and supplies exactly the missing half of the reduction above: it proves an artifact READABLE — opens it, mode-checks, decodes the envelope, verifies the checksum, and runs assertGenerationInvariants bound to the CALLER'S id — rather than merely manifest-retained. So the correction's "a generation an existing store read has just returned as USABLE" now has a concrete, store-owned API behind it, which it did not when the correction was written.

T-011 therefore ships: readGeneration(id) === "ok" -> assertHeld() -> createPin, all inside ONE serialized single-writer queue turn with no awaits between the check and the commit. The honesty of that sequence rests on the QUEUE DISCIPLINE (single writer, serialized turn, authority asserted immediately before the commit), NOT on a property of readGeneration — readGeneration proves the artifact was readable AT THAT MOMENT, and stating it any more strongly would repeat the exact substitution this issue's correction section exists to record.

The typed refusal must distinguish `not-retained` (nothing authorizes this id) from `gone` (authorized, but the artifact is absent or unusable). Collapsing them discards the distinction readGeneration exists to make.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-05 against the built store, so the remaining defect is measured rather than argued: readGeneration("g-ghost") returns not-retained, yet createPin for that same id SUCCEEDS, and the next collectGarbage silently removes the pin it just accepted.

## Suggested resolution (unchanged, and still owned by T-025)

Add a store-owned atomic operation that establishes the generation is a usable artifact and creates the pin under the same held authority and the same serialized mutation bracket, rather than two calls a caller composes. Test matrix: absent, symlinked, wrong-mode, malformed envelope, checksum-invalid, manifest-retained-but-file-missing, post-start corruption of a retained artifact, and the valid-unreferenced race. Assign it to the store ticket (T-025) rather than to T-011, and prohibit service code from re-implementing any of those checks.
title: createPin accepts any generationId — no store operation can validate-then-pin, so N-008 5a's "the service validates" has no implementation
